answer: A cedar mead hall gives each agent one cedar cask and one kettle over a banked ember. The agent gathers flower nectar from one marked meadow each morning, simmers it over the ember, and seals the batch in the cask with a numbered cedar plug. A taster opens one cask a week later and checks plug number and mead against the hall log; a cask with a swapped plug or thin mead loses its shelf for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended ember fires and a thousand sealed casks, and one kettle cannot brew a thousand batches before the nectar turns.
